newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Annan names French singer Macias as goodwill envoy.
newsitem.headline: Annan names French singer Macias as goodwill envoy.

text.p: French singer Enrico Macias, whose songs often preach conciliation between Jews and Arabs, was named on Friday by U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan as his first goodwill ambassador.
Macias, who was born and raised in Algeria and draws large audiences to his concerts in France and elsewhere, is meant to bring the message of the United Nations to a broader audience.
U.N. spokesman Fred Eckhard said Macias would be "designated by the secretary-general today as the first United Nations messenger for peace."
Eckhard said the secretary-general believed "we have become an aloof bureaucracy and Macias will be the first of a series of popular figures around the world to help stop that."
U.N. agencies, such as UNICEF, have frequently used entertainers to publicise their message but the secretary-general's office has not done so in the past.

The handsome, well-dressed Macias, 58, said it had long been a dream to see people united without violence. He sings in French, Arabic and Hebrew and has sold about 50 million records around the world.
His own background fits the multinational United Nations. He is a French citizen, born in Alberia to a Berber mother and a father whose family stems from Andalusia in Spain.
His trademark song is "J'ai Quitte Mon Pays" (I Left My Country) Another one of his songs goes: "I'm a Spanish Jew, an Armenian Greek, I'm a Creole Frenchman, an Arab Jew."
